items.originalSummary: Rolling coverage of the latest economic and financial news The number of vacancies at UK companies has fallen again, to their lowest level in 12 years (if you exclude the Covid-19 lockdown). The Office for National Statistics estimates that vacancy numbers fell by 22,000 in August-October to 690,000, the largest quarterly fall since May to July 2025. “The latest figures provide a mixed picture overall. The employment rate increased and the unemployment rate fell in the latest quarter, though these movements partly reflect particularly large differences in employment status between the groups entering and leaving the survey. “Over the same period, the number of workers on payroll fell. Vacancies also fell further, with the decline again concentrated in smaller businesses, which report that increased labour and operating costs are affecting their hiring decisions. “Meanwhile, regular wage growth slowed, driven by a fall in public sector wage growth, as the recent impact from the timing of pay awards has started to drop out of the numbers.” Continue reading...

items.originalSummary: New tech wealth, amassed with remarkable speed, is now washing up on British shores Sporting hoodies and white trainers rather than the gilets of London’s banker and lawyer class, tech bros can struggle to be taken seriously by the capital’s luxury property agents. “We worked with a young tech entrepreneur with a substantial budget, who agents assumed was looking to rent a one-bedroom flat,” says Jo Eccles, a buying agent who sources off-market properties for ultra-wealthy clients. But this week’s float by Anthropic, the AI developer behind the chatbot Claude, promises to bring even more credibility for the growing cohort of tech millionaires, which could breathe life into London’s ailing high-end property market .
